name: MongoDB
summary: Senior engineering loops at MongoDB are commonly reported to lean on distributed systems and database fundamentals: replication, sharding, consistency, storage engines and concurrency, alongside coding, system design and behavioural rounds.

loop.what: Background, motivation, the team's domain and your experience at scale.
tips: Have a crisp two-minute story of your most relevant system.
Know why a database company, specifically.

loop.what: Commonly reported as data-structure and algorithm problems with an emphasis on clean, correct code and edge cases.
tips: Test with edge cases out loud.

loop.what: Replication, consensus, sharding, consistency models and failure handling, often tied to how MongoDB works.
tips: Know replica set elections, write concern and read concern.
Be able to reason about shard key choice and hot spots.

loop.what: Design a data-heavy service; expect questions on the data model, partitioning and failure modes.
tips: Justify the data model and access patterns first.

loop.what: Ownership, collaboration and how you handle disagreement and failure.
tips: Prepare STAR stories with measurable results.
Show how you raised the bar beyond your own team.
